faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.a1: For Android users, look under `emulated/0/Download/colorify`. For Windows users, every generation creates a timestamped folder under the `colorify` folder inside your Documents directory (e.g. `Documents/colorify/2026-08-23_12-00-00`). The mcfunction / mcstructure files and a preview.png are saved there. The output path is also shown on the completion overlay.
faq.a2: If you're stuck, you can find a link to the legacy Colorify 6 documentation website on the About page — it contains detailed tutorials.
faq.q3: Can't connect to the WebSocket server / the game won't connect
faq.a3: On Windows, unlock the UWP app loopback first (see the tutorial link on the WebSocket page), then enable "Enable WebSocket" and disable "WebSocket Requires Encryption" in the game settings. Connect using `/connect 127.0.0.1:<port>`.
faq.a4: Make sure Colorify 7 is still running. Please check: 1. Whether Colorify has been closed. 2. Whether Colorify is running in the background (if you're on Android, consider a floating window / split-screen mode).
faq.a5: Check whether the port is already in use, or try a different port.
faq.q6: Staircase pixel art is generated incompletely
faq.a6: Staircase pixel art usually needs a lot of vertical space. Check whether the missing parts of your staircase pixel art were generated underground or above the world height limit.
faq.q7: Large chunks of the pixel art are missing
faq.a7: This is usually a loading issue. If you're using WebSocket transfer, keep flying to the generation edge to make sure the newest positions are loaded. If you're using mcfunction files, use `execute positioned x y z run function output_xxx` while flying around so the corresponding positions get loaded. If you're using mcstructure files, set a chunk loader with `/tickingarea` so the structure area stays loaded.
faq.q8: Part of the pixel art is missing (holes / stripes)
faq.a8: This may be caused by ID mismatches — your Minecraft version may be too old, or a Minecraft update may have made Colorify's palette outdated. We recommend generating mcfunction, importing it into your world and checking the errors to find the mismatched block IDs, then disabling them; or you can submit an Issue/PR for Colorify's palette. If you're on 1.19.x or so, you can try Colorify 6 and its flattening feature to work around it. Colorify 7 will not support flattening and only targets the latest Bedrock version.
faq.q9: Generation is slow or seems stuck (especially 3D models)
faq.a9: Voxelising large models takes time due to the heavy ray and voxel computation. If a model is too large, the app automatically falls back to a hollow shell to save time. Please wait for the progress bar; if it stays stuck for a long time, try a smaller model or fewer triangles.
faq.q10: The result colours don't match the image / lots of black
faq.a10: This is normally caused by palette limits: the game only has a limited set of block colours, so the closest match is used. On some models, normal/texture issues can sample the black placeholder texture — try a different model.
faq.q11: The app crashes on very large images
faq.a11: Extremely large images use a lot of memory. The app already streams output and is memory-optimised for large images, but images with tens of millions of pixels can still exceed your device's limits — resize the image first.
faq.q12: How do I import the mcstructure file into the game?
faq.a12: Copy the structure file into the `structures` folder of your world save, then load it with a Structure Block in-game, or use the `/structure load <name>` command. mcfunction files can be run via command blocks or directly in chat.
faq.q13: Importing the pack into the game fails
faq.a13: If your Colorify version is older than 6.1.1 (i.e. 6.1.0 or earlier), try renaming the pack extension from .mcaddon to .mcpack — that usually fixes it. This shouldn't happen on Colorify 6.1.1 or newer; if it does, please contact me on QQ: 2245638853.
faq.a14: This may be because your structure is too large and some areas have fallen into unloaded chunks. Set a `/tickingarea` manually so the region stays loaded, then try generating the structure again.
faq.q15: Does it support Java Edition Minecraft?
faq.a15: No. For Java Edition Minecraft, I recommend SlopeCraft.
faq.a16:
Are you using HarmonyOS?
Yes: Colorify does not support that system.
No: see the last FAQ.
faq.q17: When will iOS / macOS be supported?
faq.a17: I don't have iOS/macOS devices to debug on, so it's not supported for now.
faq.q18: I still have issues — how do I contact the author?
faq.a18: Find the author's contact info (email / QQ) on the About page, or open an Issue on the GitHub repository. When reporting, please include the generation parameters, the image/model used and the logs so we can locate the problem faster.

about.description: Colorify 7 is a desktop tool that turns images into Minecraft particle art and pixel art, and voxelises OBJ / GLB / GLTF 3D models into in-game builds. Results can be exported as mcfunction / mcstructure files, streamed straight into your game via WebSocket, or written directly into a Minecraft world save (LevelDB).
about.author: Author
about.featureParticleDesc: Turn an image into a dazzling in-game particle effect
about.featurePixelDesc: Flatten an image into flat or staircase pixel art, exported as mcfunction / mcstructure
about.featureVoxelDesc: Voxelise OBJ / GLB / GLTF models into solid or hollow Minecraft builds
about.featureWebSocketDesc: Stream block commands into your game in real time and watch the build happen
about.featureLdbDesc: Write generated blocks straight into a Minecraft world save while preserving the existing terrain (close the game first)
about.slopeCraftDesc: Map pixel art generator for Minecraft
